shared_context.chief_complaint: multiple stab wounds to the abdomen
shared_context.medical_history: homeless, intoxicated on presentation, postoperative ICU admission after exploratory laparotomy
shared_context.vitals: Initial: temperature 97.5°F (36.4°C), blood pressure 92/52 mmHg, pulse 145/min, respirations 33/min, oxygen saturation 90% on room air; next day vitals within normal limits
shared_context.exam_findings: sparse hair falling out throughout the body, rash at the corners of the mouth, multiple loose bowel movements, poor surgical wound healing with wound held together only by sutures and minimal underlying healing

snippets.output: The patient's vital signs indicate hypovolemic shock, and he suggests potential chronic alcohol use.
snippets.pattern_notes: Two parallel clinical interpretations of the patient's presentation, enumerated.

snippets.output: Sparse hair and rash suggest possible nutrient deficiencies. Loose bowel movements can be a sign of malabsorption or another underlying condition affecting nutrient absorption. Poor wound healing indicates a possible deficiency in nutrients essential for tissue repair.
snippets.pattern_notes: Enumeration of findings each pointing to nutrient deficiency interpretations.

snippets.output: Riboflavin (Vitamin B2) deficiency can cause sore throat, redness and swelling of the lining of the mouth and throat, cracks or sores on the outsides of the lips (cheilitis), and at the corners of the mouth (angular stomatitis).

Thiamine (Vitamin B1) deficiency is commonly associated with chronic alcohol use. Symptoms include beriberi and Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome, but it does not typically cause hair loss or poor wound healing.
snippets.pattern_notes: Enumerated properties of thiamine deficiency (association, symptoms, what it doesn't cause).

snippets.output: Vitamin C deficiency, known as scurvy, presents with poor wound healing, perifollicular hemorrhages, gingival disease, and can also present with rash (especially around the mouth) and hair loss.
snippets.pattern_notes: Enumerated properties/manifestations of vitamin C deficiency.

snippets.output: Vitamin D deficiency mainly affects bone health, causing rickets or osteomalacia, and is less associated with hair loss or wound healing directly.
snippets.pattern_notes: Enumerated properties of vitamin D deficiency.

snippets.output: Zinc deficiency symptoms include alopecia (hair loss), dermatitis (especially around body orifices), diarrhea, and impaired wound healing. The combination of alopecia, rash at the corners of the mouth, diarrhea, and poor wound healing is most consistent with Zinc deficiency. The most likely deficiency in this patient is Zinc.
snippets.pattern_notes: Enumerated zinc deficiency symptoms serve as premises supporting the final diagnostic conclusion that zinc is the deficiency.
